summary: The patch replaces factorize's unique levels with `lev.astype(var.dtype)` (the full, non-deduplicated level index) rather than casting the factorized uniques. This works for the reported unique-coordinate case but silently corrupts values or raises for non-unique level coordinates, since `split_labels` (codes) index into deduplicated uniques while `levels` is now the full array.

issues.description: Uses `lev.astype(var.dtype)` (full original index) as the MultiIndex levels instead of the factorized uniques `lev.factorize()[1].astype(var.dtype)`. The codes from `factorize()[0]` index into the DEDUPLICATED uniques, but levels is now the full-length array, so code->value mapping is misaligned whenever a level coordinate has duplicate values. E.g. coord a=[0,0,1]: factorize codes=[0,0,1], patch levels=[0,0,1]; reconstruction gives [0,0,0] (wrong) or pd.MultiIndex raises 'Level values must be unique'. The correct dtype-preserving fix casts the factorized uniques, not the raw index.

Behavioral regression for stacking non-unique coordinate indexes: the original `lev.factorize()` produced correct unique levels; this change breaks that path (silent data corruption or ValueError), which the reproduction test does not cover.

Dense single-line comprehension zipping level_indexes with variables.values() is hard to read; splitting the dtype cast onto its own line (as the levels post-processing) would be clearer and less error-prone.
